text.p: Switzerland's Jakob Hlasek, 32, announced his retirement from competitive tennis on Thursday, saying "it was time to turn the page".

At a news conference in Geneva, Hlasek, the winner of five singles titles, 20 in doubles and just over $5.5 million in a career that spanned 14 years, said he had made his decision in September during the U.S. Open.
"It was a difficult decision," said Hlasek, who had reached a career-high number seven in the world rankings in 1989 but seen it slip to its current 76.
"I made my choice at the U.S. Open and nothing has happened since to change my mind. It was important for me to end on a good year -- my best since 1992.
"I didn't want to be forced into retiring because of a mediocre ranking that would have prevented me from playing in big tournaments."

One of the world's leading doubles player, Hlasek's career actually came to a premature conclusion when he was forced out of world doubles championships, being played in Hartford this week, because of an injury to partner Frenchman Guy Forget. Hlasek and Forget had already won the title once before in 1990.
Althought Hlasek never advanced past the quarter-finals in grand slam singles competition, he teamed up with compatriot Marc Rosset in 1992 to win the French Open doubles crown.
For almost a decade, Hlasek and Rosset were the corner-stone of Switzerland's Davis Cup efforts. In 1992 they took the tiny Alpine nation to the finals, losing to the United States.
Earlier this year the two men led Switzerland to its first Nations Cup title.
